name: Brunei
summary: A yellow field crossed diagonally by white and black stripes, with the red national emblem in the centre: a parasol, wings, raised hands and a crescent bearing the national motto.
origin: The yellow field represents the Sultan of Brunei, and the stripes his two chief ministers. The stripes were added in 1906 under the British protectorate. The national emblem was added on 29 September 1959, with the first written constitution.

colors.name: Yellow
colors.meaning: The Sultan; yellow is the royal colour in Malay tradition.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The Pengiran Bendahara, the chief minister.

colors.name: Black
colors.meaning: The Pengiran Pemancha, the second minister.

symbols.name: Parasol (payung)
symbols.description: A royal umbrella with a flag above it.

symbols.name: Wings
symbols.meaning: The protection of justice, tranquillity, prosperity and peace.

symbols.name: Hands
symbols.description: Two raised hands on either side.
symbols.meaning: The government's duty to promote welfare, peace and prosperity.

symbols.name: Crescent with motto
symbols.description: An upturned crescent with 'Always in service with God's guidance' in Jawi script, above a ribbon reading 'Brunei Darussalam'.

history.label: Protectorate flag
history.note: Yellow with white and black stripes.

facts: Brunei is one of the world's few remaining absolute monarchies.
The white stripe is slightly wider than the black one.
clues: Yellow with diagonal white and black stripes and a red emblem with a parasol and two hands.
Its stripes stand for two chief ministers.
Its yellow is the colour of its sultan.
